title: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
short_summary: The Presentation of Mary celebrates her complete dedication to God from the beginning of her life. Its narrative image comes from the ancient Protoevangelium of James, which says that Joachim and Anne brought the young Mary to the Temple, while the liturgy focuses on her lifelong readiness for God's call.
key_facts: The memorial is celebrated on November 21.
The presentation story is not narrated in the canonical Gospels.
Its earliest written source is the second-century Protoevangelium of James.
The feast was celebrated in Jerusalem and the Byzantine East before spreading to the West.

sections.heading: The traditional story
sections.body: The Protoevangelium of James relates that Joachim and Anne, grateful for the birth of their daughter, brought Mary to the Temple at the age of three to fulfill a vow. She remained there in a life devoted to God until the time of her betrothal to Joseph. The work is an early Christian apocryphal text, not part of Scripture, but several names and scenes from it entered Christian art and devotion.

sections.heading: Growth of the feast
sections.body: An anniversary of the dedication of a Marian church near the Jerusalem Temple in 543 became associated with Mary's entry into the Temple. The celebration spread widely in the Byzantine world. It appeared in the West during the Middle Ages, was temporarily removed from the Roman calendar, and was restored in the sixteenth century.

sections.heading: What the liturgy celebrates
sections.body: The memorial does not require the apocryphal narrative to be read as documentary history. Its enduring subject is Mary's consecration to God. The canonical Gospels portray her listening to God's word, consenting to the Annunciation, following her Son, and standing with the disciples as the Church awaits the Holy Spirit.

sections.heading: A day of dedication
sections.body: The feast became especially important to religious communities and to Christians who understood their vocation as a presentation of their whole life to God. It invites every baptized person to see holiness not as a single dramatic moment but as a life gradually made available to grace.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Scripture and tradition
catholic_connection_sections.body: Catholic devotion can preserve a traditional image without treating an apocryphal writing as canonical Scripture. The feast's theological meaning rests on Mary's biblical vocation and her complete response to God.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: A life offered to God
catholic_connection_sections.body: Mary's dedication points to the baptismal calling shared by all Christians. Particular religious vows make that self-offering visible, but the call to belong wholly to God is universal.

historical_cautions: The Protoevangelium of James is not canonical Scripture and its Temple narrative should not be stated as verified biography.
The connection between the 543 church dedication and the present feast developed over time.
